pages.title: Eye structures and the path of light

images.alt: From a change to a meaning. The original stimulus and the neural signal are different forms of information.
The main structures of the eye. Follow the light from the cornea at the front to the retina at the back. The optic nerve is an output pathway, not part of the incoming light route.
Accommodation in the source diagram. Compare the flatter lens for a distant object with the rounder lens for a nearby object. Refraction by the cornea is also essential.
Predict the focus before choosing the lens. A diverging correction helps the myopia model; a converging correction helps the hyperopia model. Dots indicate model focal positions.

Different directions: light and information. Light passes ganglion and bipolar layers to reach photoreceptors. Information returns through bipolar pathways to ganglion cells. Cell numbers and connections are schematic.
The retina in cross-section. The photoreceptor layer lies toward the pigmented backing. Ganglion-cell axons gather into the optic nerve.
Outer, middle and inner ear. Locate the air-filled middle ear and the fluid-filled inner ear before tracing the conducting structures.
Inside the cochlea. Follow the magnification from the cochlea to the organ of Corti. Relative movement of the basilar and tectorial structures bends hair-cell projections.
Frequency is not amplitude. More cycles in the same time indicate higher frequency. A larger wave excursion indicates greater amplitude. These are illustrative waves, not recorded measurements.
Different balance mechanisms. The canal cupula is distinct from the otolithic membrane containing calcium-carbonate particles. This is a comparison of mechanisms, not a dissection view.
From tongue surface to taste receptor cells. Taste buds contain receptor cells that respond to dissolved chemicals. They are not exclusive sweet, sour, salty, bitter or umami regions.
The olfactory sensory region. Odour molecules reach receptors in the nasal region; their neurons send input toward the olfactory bulb.
